adam-pasteswitch.summary: AnimateClipper testnet and Zig mainnet contracts mirror C2 rotation; a balanceOf getter conceals address resolution.
adam-pasteswitch.limitation: 36 mirrored changes describe configuration writes, not victims or fund transfers. The broader PasteSwitch branches do not all use blockchain; the Zig contract also appears in Talos.

async-dd.summary: Independently analyzes IPFS staging and decrypted Ethereum RPC and contract settings.
async-dd.limitation: Configured fallbacks and active delivery are labeled separately.

async-ms.title: Unpacking the AsyncAPI npm supply-chain compromise
async-ms.summary: Documents two IPFS staging objects and distinguishes active import-time execution from disabled malware modules.
async-ms.limitation: Credential harvesting, encrypted exfiltration and propagation modules were implemented but disabled in the analyzed build.

async-step.title: Coordinated AsyncAPI supply-chain attack: Miasma RAT
async-step.summary: Combines sandbox observations of IPFS delivery with multi-channel fallback configuration.
async-step.limitation: Ethereum configuration does not prove an on-chain command exchange during observation.

bdns.summary: Primary evidence for blockchain dns for c2 and delivery, emercoin naming for malicious infrastructure.

bizone-rtm.title: RTM: banking malware analysis
bizone-rtm.summary: Original Russian-language analysis of transaction-amount signaling and alternative Namecoin resolution.
bizone-rtm.limitation: Historical API and resolver examples are not statements of current availability.

blockchairdocs.title: Blockchair API documentation
blockchairdocs.summary: Protocol or provider reference for the documented baseline surface.

bscdocs.title: BNB Smart Chain RPC endpoint directory

canister.title: TeamPCP deploys CanisterWorm on npm
canister.summary: Primary evidence for icp canister as a dead-drop resolver.

checkmarx-contract.title: Supply-chain attack using Ethereum smart contracts to distribute multi-platform malware
checkmarx-contract.summary: A malicious npm preinstall hook uses contract lookup data for platform-specific payload retrieval.

confiant-hexmage.title: Skimming on the Blockchain: A Magecart Campaign That Uses EtherHiding, Found by Malvertising Scanning
confiant-hexmage.summary: HexMage traffic captures link Sepolia contracts to off-chain skimmer delivery and GET-based collection.
confiant-hexmage.limitation: Primary HexMage traffic captures + contract reads. Store-specific contracts return bare hostname or encrypted hostname envelope; loader supplies path. Offchain card exfil; only Fetch-GET enabled in decoded configs. WebSocket/beacon/image exfil code exists but not observed. Same-toolkit overlap with SourceDefense not resolved; no VexTrio attribution. Merchants are victims, never blocklist labels. Split encrypted-envelope parser branch not seen used.

dark-utilities.title: Dark Utilities: malicious campaigns from C2-as-a-service
dark-utilities.summary: Identifies IPFS-hosted Windows and Linux payloads used by a C2 service.

deadlock.title: DeadLock: smart contracts for malicious purposes
deadlock.summary: Primary evidence for ransomware communication proxy discovery.

deadvax.title: Dead#Vax: multi-stage VHD delivery and self-parsing batch scripts
deadvax.summary: Documents an IPFS-hosted VHD in a multistage AsyncRAT delivery chain.
deadvax.limitation: This establishes IPFS payload hosting, not IPFS C2 or ledger exfiltration.

dfir.title: EtherRAT and TukTuk before The Gentlemen ransomware
dfir.summary: Primary evidence for arweave-backed configuration recovery.

elastic-revstealer.title: REVSTEALER ramps up: analysis of up-and-coming infostealer
elastic-revstealer.summary: Encrypted Polygon fallback resolves C2; follow-on modules also retrieve settings and mining arguments from contracts.
elastic-revstealer.limitation: Contracts and provider lists recovered from samples are code evidence. Malware distribution telemetry does not prove every configured route executed.

elastic-revstealer-paper.title: REVSTEALER technical white paper
elastic-revstealer-paper.summary: Technical supplement publishes provider fallback pools, selectors and encrypted settings used by analyzed REVSTEALER builds.
elastic-revstealer-paper.limitation: Companion to the same Elastic investigation, not an additional ranking vote.

eset-rtm.title: Read The Manual: banking malware research
eset-rtm.summary: Original RTM report includes .bit infrastructure and third-party resolver behavior.
eset-rtm.limitation: The report describes disruption of resolution after disclosure; names and resolvers are historical.

etherrat.title: EtherRAT: Ethereum contract resolution and RPC voting
etherrat.summary: Primary evidence for contract-based c2 address resolution.

ethplorerdocs.title: Ethplorer and Binplorer API base addresses
ethplorerdocs.summary: Protocol or provider reference for the documented baseline surface.

expel-clearfake.title: ClearFake: new LOTL techniques
expel-clearfake.summary: Documents BSC testnet contract stages, platform routing and a visitor UUID check.
expel-clearfake.limitation: UUID records do not establish a count of unique infected devices.

filescan-redline.title: EtherHiding Under the Hood: On-Chain Forensics Beyond the Public Disclosure
filescan-redline.summary: Static sample analysis and decrypted contract history reconstruct a BSC resolver and historical C2 changes.
filescan-redline.limitation: Static reversing of six corpus samples + decrypted on-chain history; unknown initial delivery and missing reflective loader; RedLine/META exact brand unresolved. 122 bytecode-identical contracts are candidate infrastructure, not proven same campaign. Reuses SectopRAT resolver but attribution remains unknown.

forcememo.title: ForceMemo: GitHub Python repositories compromised via account takeover
forcememo.summary: Documents Solana fallback RPC configuration and a controlled run reaching an off-chain payload server.
forcememo.limitation: A configured RPC fallback does not mean every provider was contacted in the run.

gelato-etherhiding.title: From Blockchain to Clipboard: Dissecting an EtherHiding ClickFix Attack
gelato-etherhiding.summary: Polygon resolver reads precede a fingerprinted clipboard-execution lure.
gelato-etherhiding.limitation: Own browser observation + script analysis. Initial compromise and final stealer identity not established. Generic RPC examples and detection query domain arrays are not observed endpoints. Theburritocity.com is a victim; 45.86.230.47 appears with victim telemetry, not established as C2. Proposed Defender queries reference undefined Web3Devices variable and need correction/validation before reuse.

guardio.title: EtherHiding: hiding malicious code in smart contracts
guardio.summary: Primary evidence for smart-contract payload hosting.

hashhiding.title: XCTDH adopts Hash Hiding
hashhiding.summary: Primary evidence for recipient-address c2 signaling.

hunt-gentlemen.title: The Gentlemen Affiliate Deploys EtherRAT Across Windows Networks Using Ethereum Smart Contract C2
hunt-gentlemen.summary: Recovered EtherRAT toolkit resolves C2 through an Ethereum contract, with seven configured public RPC providers and periodic refresh.
hunt-gentlemen.limitation: Primary recovered open-directory/toolkit analysis plus historical contract reconstruction; Huntress/Sysdig references are corroboration, not extra independent cases. The Gentlemen affiliation assessed; does not verify Sysdig DPRK link. Non-EtherRAT reverse-shell/proxy IPs must not be mislabeled blockchain RPC. Registry-hive exfiltration is ordinary off-chain HTTP.

hunter-sliver.title: Sliver C2 Windows Post-Exploitation Staging, 193.233.202.17
hunter-sliver.summary: Reverse engineering of an Ethereum-resolving Node implant alongside a separate conventional Sliver strand.
hunter-sliver.limitation: Explicitly reuses Hunt.io’s historical indicators; adds analysis, not a new incident. Prepared scripts do not establish execution and the Sliver IP is not a blockchain RPC.

netskope-webrtc.title: Malware on the Blockchain: An Ongoing Campaign’s New WebRTC Twist
netskope-webrtc.summary: A BSC-testnet loader stages browser WebRTC code that receives another payload over UDP.
netskope-webrtc.limitation: Observed compromised-site telemetry plus WebRTC stager code analysis. No actor/family attribution. This BSC-testnet cluster is related by delivery model to Base/Amatera, not proven same actor. Forge SDP answer bypasses external signaling; do not claim no DTLS/ICE network handshake. Exact full RPC pool not printed in article/IOC text. Two injected loader URLs are compromised websites, not dedicated malicious domains.

netskope-webrtc-iocs.title: Amatera ClickFix: published IOC supplement
netskope-webrtc-iocs.summary: Official companion IOC list for the BSC-testnet/WebRTC investigation.
netskope-webrtc-iocs.limitation: Supplement to the same investigation, not an extra ranking vote. Compromised-site paths are excluded from dedicated-infrastructure labels.

nglite.title: NGLite in a targeted attack campaign

nknshell.title: NKNShell malware distributed via VPN website

powerstar.limitation: The hardcoded gateway list is configuration evidence; it does not prove every gateway received traffic.

sd-polygon.summary: Polygon-backed configuration leads to checkout interception and off-chain image-like data requests.
sd-polygon.limitation: Blob execution is not a universal bypass of Content Security Policy.

sd-tracker.limitation: This project imports the dated table as a historical snapshot; current ownership and liveness are untested.
